basics.name: Maoqi Liu
basics.label: Graduate Student in Artificial Intelligence
basics.summary: First-year graduate student at the School of Artificial Intelligence, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. Research focuses on Post-Training and Continual Learning in Large Language Models.

work.name: ByteDance
work.summary: Douyin E-commerce Customer Service team, mentored by Junwei He. Solely responsible for full-scenario RL post-training for customer service single-Agent architecture.
highlights: Data Construction: Back-traced training & reward annotation data from online sessions with real actions and final outcomes; improved good-outcome annotation consistency from 14% to 90%+.

Solution Reward: Modeled issue resolution with distilled small RM (F1 0.86) and TabPFN correlation mining; decomposed trajectory-level rewards into step-level actions for fine-grained credit assignment.
Experience Reward: Converted pointwise scoring to role-swapped pairwise comparison with business protocol constraints, boosting intra-group reward ranking for GRPO advantage estimation.
Training & Deployment: GRPO training with dual rewards deployed to pre-sales scenarios: session resolution +3.2pp, experience +2pp, interaction blockage rate -7pp.
Research: Proposed protocol-level rubrics ProRubric to mitigate reward hacking (First Author, under review) and co-authored Agentic RL with TabPFN credit assignment.

volunteer.summary: Over 100 hours of volunteer service, actively supporting community initiatives and providing daily assistance to fellow students.

publications.name: Scoring Higher, Answering Worse: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL via Protocol-Level Rubrics
publications.summary: Maoqi Liu, Junwei He, Bowen Zhang, Feiran Li, Wentao Ma, Rongyi Lin, Shuhan Zhong, Quan Fang. First Author. Identifies that reward hacking in Rubric-RL stems from compensatory linear weighted sum rather than criteria design. Proposes reorganizing rubrics into protocol-level dimensions where scores are awarded only when full protocol conditions are met without vetoes, achieving +10.8 appropriateness gain and outperforming all baselines across 7 benchmarks.

publications.name: CoDe-LoRA: Mitigating the Orthogonality Dilemma in Continual Learning of LLMs via Knowledge Consolidation and Decoupling
publications.summary: Maoqi Liu, Quan Fang, Yufei He. First Author. Identifies the orthogonality dilemma in continual learning of LLMs, where strict orthogonal isolation discards shared knowledge. Proposes a replay-free dual-branch LoRA consolidating commonalities via adaptive null-space projection and decoupling task-specific features via prototype semantic routing, reaching 80.6% average accuracy and +7.0 over O-LoRA.

publications.name: NOTAM-Evolve: A Knowledge-Guided Self-Evolving Optimization Framework with LLMs for NOTAM Interpretation
publications.summary: Maoqi Liu, Quan Fang, Yuhao Wu, Can Zhao, Yang Yang, Kaiquan Cai. First Author. Accurately interpreting NOTAMs requires dynamic knowledge grounding and regulation-based reasoning. Proposes knowledge-graph-guided retrieval combined with iterative SFT/DPO self-evolution, improving 7B model accuracy from 0.458 to 0.762.

publications.name: Knots: A Large-Scale Multi-Agent Enhanced Expert-Annotated Dataset and LLM Prompt Optimization for NOTAM Semantic Parsing
publications.summary: Maoqi Liu, Quan Fang, Yang Yang, et al. First Author. Advances NOTAM analysis from surface extraction to domain semantic parsing. Constructs a benchmark of 12,347 expert-annotated NOTAMs across 194 FIRs using a multi-agent debate framework (F1 92% vs 57% baseline).

publications.name: R²A²-MoE: Ridge Regression-based Analytic Adaptation with Mixture of Experts for Continual Learning with Vision-Language Models
publications.summary: Maoqi Liu, et al. First Author. Proposes Ridge Regression-based Analytic Adaptation with Mixture of Experts for VLMs, mitigating dual forgetting through closed-form expert optimization.

projects.name: Job Recommendation System Based on Knowledge Graphs
